A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEDIC framework and share the same experimental core. Their text, figures, tables, algorithm, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations across clinical and general benchmarks, including CEF scores, MEDEC results, and pairwise Elo rankings (Tables 2 and 4; Figures 3–5).

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical evaluations and adds a clinician-versus-LLM-judge comparison on 73 open-ended questions (Appendix A.1, Table 4).

M1.justification: MEDIC's evaluation procedures and CEF's YES-only question generation, bidirectional verification, four scores, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Added validation and inference documentation do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: The benchmark and task coverage in Appendix A.3 is retained. The clinician study uses a subset of existing open-ended clinical responses. FRANK evaluations and the YES-only ablation are attributed to prior work, rather than newly conducted benchmark evaluations here.

E2.justification: v3 introduces clinician ratings as a reference comparator for the three existing LLM judges in Appendix A.1/Table 4. The benchmark model roster and comparator membership in the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added validation study uses one practicing clinician, 73 questions, responses sampled across study models, and three clinical rating axes on 1–5 scales. Existing benchmark protocols are retained; the new decoding tables and prompt templates disclose settings without establishing changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a direct clinician-agreement study, substantially extending evaluator validation beyond v2's agreement between LLM judges and metric correlations. Existing analyses and the SOAP case study remain. The newly summarized YES-only ablation is explicitly attributed to prior work.

E5.justification: Table 4 introduces clinician–judge mean-difference estimates with 95% confidence intervals and explicit interpretations of whether intervals include zero. Existing Elo confidence intervals and match-count reporting remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds nine clinician–judge comparison outcomes, including Qwen's practicality/feasibility difference of -1.14 (95% CI: -1.46 to -0.81). The full benchmark table (v2 Table 4, v3 Table 5) and MEDEC results are unchanged. New Table 2 redisplays selected existing scores.

T1.justification: CEF's score definitions and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical content. The additional validation arguments and YES-only motivation introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction newly states that leading indicators do not predict deployment outcomes, qualifying v2's predictive framing, although predictive wording remains elsewhere in that paragraph. The central knowledge-execution gap, passive-versus-active safety, and portfolio-selection claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges the absence of formal clinician-panel taxonomy validation and adds a specific prompt-sensitivity limitation. Sections 3.2–3.5 also make stronger interpretations connecting clinician agreement to CEF validity and Elo correctness, while Appendix A.4 adds a rationale for YES-only questions.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility information through task-specific judge and generation parameters (Tables 6–7), generation prompts and scoring rubrics (Appendix A.7), and consolidated code/data access information (Appendix A.6, Table 9). v2 supplied only a subset of these details.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Raha et al. (2026), Pagnoni et al. (2021), and Christophe et al. (2026). It expands discussion of MEDIC's relationship to clinician-validated frameworks such as MedHELM and HealthBench; most existing related-work content is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive localized revisions, explanatory paragraphs are added, and author/affiliation information changes. Appendices gain validation and resources sections, with the model list relocated and prompts expanded. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual documentation with knowledge-versus-execution and clinician-comparison tables, decoding-parameter and data-link tables, and four illustrative leaderboard screenshots. The author block is reformatted and existing displays move. The original quantitative plots and results tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The added decoding settings, prompts, and resource information make the evaluations easier to reproduce and audit, while the clinician study provides a human reference absent from v2. These gains are tempered by overinterpreting a one-clinician, 73-question mean-score comparison as establishing CEF validity and Elo correctness in Sections 3.2–3.5. The overall improvement is therefore limited.
